tasks.task: Run a technical SEO audit and rank the fixes

items.when: When you have a crawl export and Search Console exports and need fixes ranked by impact
When the crawler lists thousands of issues and you must cut them to the few that matter
When you want a second audit of crawling, indexing and structure to compare with yours
When the site is an online shop and the crawl must become five to ten ranked fixes
When the client wants the audit and the first on-page fixes done in one run
Before fixes go in, to save the site's state so later changes can be seen

tasks.task: Find why pages are not indexed and list the fixes

items.when: When the indexing report shows many excluded pages and each reason needs a decision
When you have a Search Console export and need to know why pages stay out of the index
When a shop has empty or very short pages that may be dragging the rest down

tasks.task: Build a keyword map by search intent

items.when: When searches need grouping by intent, scoring and assigning one group to each page
Before any keyword tool, to start from the questions customers really ask
When you want a second grouping of the same topic by intent to compare
When the site is a shop and each collection and product needs its own topic
When you must judge the chance of winning a group against the sites that rank now
When the list is built from search volume alone, to go back to what buyers want to know

tasks.task: Write an SEO content brief for a new or refreshed page

items.when: Before you write or rewrite, to match page type and angle to what already ranks
When a writer needs one page built from the live results and the client's customer words
When you have the ranking pages and want a second brief with gaps to compare
When the brief needs a one-page outline with headings in the order a reader asks
When you need to read what ranks and what is cited for the query, with links
When the brief lists twenty headings and no point, to find the one focus

tasks.task: Write or refresh a post to win a search

items.when: Before drafting, so the post follows a brief built from the live results
When one search matters and the post must be better than what ranks today
When you need a long post with the answer first, FAQs and internal links
When the title is flat, to get several angles that earn the click honestly
When an old post buries its answer, to rewrite each section answer first
Before publishing, to check the draft against its brief for facts, voice and structure

tasks.task: Rewrite titles and meta descriptions for low click-through

items.when: When a page has many impressions but a low click rate for its average position
Before rewriting, to pick the pages where a better title would pay most this month
When you want three title and description pairs inside the length limits to choose from
When a title is chosen, to check it picks the right searcher and promises a clear gain

tasks.task: Plan internal links to lift a page that matters

items.when: When a key page ranks lower than it should, sits deep, or has just gone live
When the whole site needs a map of which pages link to which, with anchor text
When links should follow a hub of one main page and its supporting pages
When the menu and URL structure are the reason pages sit too deep

tasks.task: Draft structured data for the main page types

items.when: When a page type Google supports needs JSON-LD, or the home page needs business markup
When you want checked markup for a named page type, ready to paste

tasks.task: Diagnose a drop in organic search traffic

items.when: When organic traffic falls and you must work through the causes step by step
When you have the Search Console export and need the pages that lost clicks and why
When the client wants the diagnosis, the fixes and a check that traffic came back
When the drop may be a tracking or channel-labelling change, not a search change
When you already have a favourite cause, to keep the facts that do not fit it

tasks.task: Tell a client what a Google core update did to their site

items.when: After a core update finishes rolling out, to say plainly what happened and what to do
Before the read-out, to find which pages and queries moved across the update dates
When the update hit thin or overlapping pages and each needs a keep, merge or cut call
When one scary percentage leads the read-out, to ask what it counts and against what

tasks.task: Run the monthly search review and report

items.when: In the first week of each month, once last month's Search Console data has settled
Each month, to turn the export into pages to push, thin pages and what changed
When the client needs non-branded clicks against last period in a short report
When the report should end with the few pages worth pushing this month
When analytics and Search Console disagree on what counts as organic search

tasks.task: Find decaying content and refresh, merge or cut it

items.when: Every quarter, to pick the posts to refresh and run them through in order
When a blog has many old posts and each needs a refresh, merge or cut decision
When you have the list of posts and need to know how deep each update should go
Before anything is deleted, to mark each page keep, update, merge or redirect
When a refreshed post should lead with its answer so search and AI tools can quote it

tasks.task: Plan a site migration without losing traffic

items.when: Before any change of domain, URL structure, platform or templates
When content moves from an old site to a new one and rank and links must be kept
When several domains and subdomains need one layout and one set of redirect rules
After launch, to find redirects that chain or all point at one page
Before and after launch, to compare tags, pages and rankings and catch what broke

tasks.task: Write a 90-day SEO plan from a Search Console export

items.when: Before planning, to test whether search can pay for this business at all
When the plan needs the few searches worth chasing, scored by value and effort
When the first month should be pages already close to page one
When you need search overlap and content depth against named rivals
When the plan assumes search is the channel, to check where the audience really goes

tasks.task: List on-page fixes for the top pages

items.when: When one page needs fixes for title, headings, content and links in one list
When the fix list includes titles and descriptions with low click rates
When a top page needs more links from the rest of the site
When a page will not rise, to check its type still matches what ranks

tasks.task: Plan and write collection and product pages for a shop

items.when: When a shop has products and a keyword export and needs collections that match buying searches
When one collection needs its title, heading, URL, copy and FAQ written
When one product page needs layout, copy, image names and markup for a target term
When each collection needs three title options to pick from
When collection copy reads like filler, to test it and get a true, specific rewrite

tasks.task: Write a fair comparison or best-of page

items.when: When you have rivals and product facts and want pages people and AI tools quote
Before writing, to choose between best-of, review, alternative and versus pages
When a buyer question needs a fair ranked list with real numbers
Before choosing the page type, to see which kind already ranks for the query
Before publishing, to check every claim about a rival is supported

tasks.task: Plan how to be named by AI assistants

items.when: First, to score how likely AI search is to cite the site and why
When a shop wants a baseline of who AI names, the gaps and a plan to close them
When one page or topic needs edits so AI tools can quote it
When you need the sites AI tools keep citing for the buyer's questions
When the robots file blocks AI crawlers the client wants to allow

tasks.task: Read out Core Web Vitals for the pages that matter

items.when: When speed is one part of the audit and must be ranked against the other fixes
When a slow site needs its Core Web Vitals, bundle and caching problems found

tasks.task: Audit the Google profile and plan local search work

items.when: When a local or service-area business needs a listing audit and ranked fixes
When many area pages are needed and each must be useful, not a copy
When the home or contact page needs local business markup
When the listing needs a steady, honest rhythm of new reviews and replies
When area pages exist, to find the ones too short or too alike to keep

tasks.task: Plan link earning and outreach

items.when: When the client has something worth citing and wants links without buying them
When links should come from digital PR, brand mentions and local sources together
When a shop needs to see which links rivals have that it lacks
Before outreach is sent, to test each claim and the legal basics of the email

tasks.task: Plan a topic cluster from keywords to briefs

items.when: When one topic should become a main page, supporting posts, briefs and links
Before the cluster, so each page in it owns one group of searches
When the cluster needs its URL structure and linking set out

tasks.task: Plan search set-up for more than one language or country

items.when: When the site adds markets and needs language URLs and the tags that link them
After launch, to check the language versions are crawled and indexed as planned

always.when: When a page or report states a number or fact you cannot trace to a source
Before a brief, page or report is sent, to catch typos and terms used two ways

helpers.when: When briefs are agreed and the posts and guides must be written at volume
When link earning becomes a campaign with a prospect list and many emails
When the main goal is to be named by AI assistants, not to rank in Google
When fixes need template, rendering or page speed changes in the code
When the job is mostly the map listing, local directories and reviews
When the client asks what search is worth next to paid, email and other channels

gaps: No library item builds a page-by-page redirect map from an old crawl and a new one, with a launch-day checklist
No library item reads a Core Web Vitals field report for search pages; the speed items are written for developers
No library item writes a core update read-out for a client; only the kit prompt does
No library item finds two or more pages competing for the same search
No library item reads server logs to show what search and AI crawlers fetch
No library item checks whether pages built with JavaScript are rendered and indexed
No library item forecasts the traffic and revenue a ranking gain would bring
No library item checks name, address and phone across listings or plans photos and posts for a Google profile
No library item checks a page against Google's people-first content questions and author signals
No library item audits language and country tags on a live multi-language site
No library item checks the live results page for intent outside the kit prompt
